body:
## What to build

Keep a lazy SQLite Margin result with a public TRUE or FALSE column usable on either side of ordinary joins and set operations. Its public schema and values must remain queryable when another relation consumes it, while derived-result type and order semantics remain delegated to dbplyr.

On current main 978d7bef4247bf1348af5b90bfab47924db25500, a one-row source has g equal to a and integer TRUE payload 7. Expanding a rollup of g succeeds directly and after head. Joining a key-only source to that result raises “no such column: TRUE”; putting the expanded result on the left also fails. The same joins over the original source and an explicitly computed expansion succeed with the public TRUE column and expected values.

Union-all and union succeed with the expansion on the left but fail with it on the right. Intersect and set difference fail on either side. A 48-observation comparison of sixteen compositions over source, materialized, and expanded inputs found ten expanded-input failures and successful source/materialized controls throughout. An independent witness with FALSE payload 19 reproduced both join failures, the union-all right-input failure, and intersection failure; its expected-behavior assertion exited 1.

Two observations distinguish the mechanisms. A left-input join retains the special SQLite result class, but its multi-input query graph is not traversed by alias repair; explicitly applying the existing repair helper still leaves it failing. A right-input union loses that class, and applying the helper explicitly makes it execute. These are evidence for implementation work, not a prescription to expose private classes or helpers publicly.

Closed #1095 and merged #1134 repaired ordinary limiting/filtering and select/union layers. Closed #826 covered the direct boundary. This ticket covers binary relation graphs and either input position, which remained broken after those fixes. It does not require preserving Margin order or direct-result type guarantees after an ordinary derived verb, nor implicit materialization.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both input positions of supported ordinary joins over Boolean-word Margin results remain collectable, with the expected public names, values and row counts.
- [ ] Both input positions of union-all, union, intersection and set difference remain usable; preserve their ordinary bag/set semantics.
- [ ] Cover TRUE, FALSE and mixed-case public spellings, and include empty/populated fixtures and representative column roles, label choices and Margin-order choices.
- [ ] Live SQLite regressions include successful original-source and explicitly materialized-result controls, plus cases that distinguish class loss from an untraversed multi-input graph.
- [ ] Direct collection/materialization and the limiting/filtering behavior fixed by #1095 retain their existing guarantees, including alias collision safety.
- [ ] Construction and query repair add no unrequested source-data read or implicit materialization, consistent with ADR 0020; derived-result types and order retain ADR 0031's ordinary dbplyr semantics.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

Investigated on 2026-11-02 using R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dbplyr 2.6.0 and RSQLite 3.53.3 on macOS arm64, against the SHA above. A fresh fetch confirmed that main still named that SHA before publication. Fixtures used private in-memory SQLite databases; no implementation fix was made.

Duplicate searches covered open and closed issues for Boolean, Boolean join, Boolean union, SQLite join, SQLite intersect and SQLite composition, plus relevant Boolean SQLite pull requests. The complete bodies/comments of #1095, #826 and #976 and the #1134 discussion were checked. No separate report for this binary-graph boundary was found. The [dated investigation](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/db5d3e0c5c4fd2f418f89cabd9bf7d682e20e006/investigation/expand-grouping-greedy-hunt-2026-11-02.md) records S1 and the complete scope/limits. The [primary expected-behavior replay](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/db5d3e0c5c4fd2f418f89cabd9bf7d682e20e006/investigation/2026-11-02-expand-grouping-greedy/local/sql-alias-graph.R) and [independent witness](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/db5d3e0c5c4fd2f418f89cabd9bf7d682e20e006/investigation/2026-11-02-expand-grouping-greedy/sql/independent-alias-graph.R), with adjacent logs and CSVs, are pinned to the published evidence commit. Both expected-behavior assertion modes intentionally fail on the investigated baseline. PR #1137 records the investigation change and its verification/review records; it does not fix this ticket.

comments.body: Implemented in #1150. The PR contains the verification and Standards/Spec review records.

title: [P2] Keep SQLite Boolean-word Margin results usable as binary query inputs
